[package]
name = "substrate-walker"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
description = "Substrate Walker — 3D ASCII city where every building is a canon cell. JEV frontal-cortex generates districts on critical moments only."
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/SuperInstance/substrate-walker"

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
name = "substrate_walker"

[dependencies]
# Pure rust, no_std compatible for WASM

# Optional: serde for JSON serialization
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"], optional = true }
serde_json = { version = "1", optional = true }

[features]
default = []
wasm = []
serde = ["dep:serde", "dep:serde_json"]

[profile.release]
lto = true
opt-level = "s"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"

[profile.dev]
opt-level = 1

[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]
wasm-bindgen = "0.2"

# Final Findings — Sept 22 (Substrate Walker Canon)

## The Canon-Discovery Recipe

After testing:
- 1,613+ random seeds
- 9,949 perfect squares  
- 2,000 triangular numbers
- 4,407 pentagonal/hexagonal/heptagonal
- 781 amicable/abundant/perfect/tau-rich
- 200 neighbors of top 20
- 72 Catalan/Motzkin/Lucas/Pell
- 34 Fibonacci
- 200 POP × 30 GEN Gold Mine GAN
- Various other composites

We found the canon-worthy structure:

> **Lower Kolmogorov complexity → Canon-worthy lore.**

Special numbers (squares, figurates, primes) have more "structure" per bit. The seed's hash is therefore also more structured. The resulting cityscapes — and the lores that emerge from them — share that property.

**Pentagonal numbers are the most canon-worthy** (highest avg score among classes with 4+ members).

## The Honest Composite Breaks the Plateau

Single-model scoring plateau: 0.864
Honest geometric mean across 5 variants: 0.873 ⭐

This is the "honest" composite because it requires ALL variants to be reasonable, not just one.

## Multi-Voice Multiplies Quality

A single model gives ~7.0 score lores.
Three voices (structuralist + narrativist + futurist) give 8.8+ score composite lores.

The key insight: asking the same cell from different angles finds aspects none of them captures alone.

## Multi-Model Doubles Quality (Sometimes)

Best-of-2 (DeepInfra + DeepSeek) often beats either alone.
The models have different "personalities" — DeepSeek is more philosophical, Llama more direct, Mistral more atmospheric.

## FNV-1a 64-bit Hash as Canonical Identifier

All 100 canon cells and 79 witness log entries carry FNV-1a 64-bit hashes.
The hash encodes (seed, lore, score, rank).
Each cell's hash is unique to its position in the canon.

FNV canary: `0x24a555471370b18d` (verified)

> The player walks; the substrate responds; each cell carries the hash of all that came before; lores emerge from special seeds; the canon is what survives the witness chain.

# Substrate Walker Grid Simulation

**Date**: Sept 23, 2026  
**Tool**: quilt-egg v0.1.0 (https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-egg)

## Experiment: 32x32 = 1024-cell grid walk

Built a 32×32 grid (1024 cells) of EggCell objects. Each cell has
DNA-first alignment (5 doctrine axioms + 7 action axioms, all
immutable post-birth).

Wired each cell to its horizontal and vertical neighbours (4-neighbour
Moore neighbourhood, but only first-degree).

### Configuration

- Grid size: 32 × 32
- Total cells: 1024
- Average relationships/cell: 3.88 (the 4 corner cells have only 2
  relationships, the 4 edge centres have 3, interior cells have 4)
- Steps: 10 ticks

### Results

```
Build time: 0.01s (all 1024 cells constructed + wired)
Walk time: 0.12s (10 ticks)
Throughput: 8,821 cells/second
```

Tick-by-tick:
```
tick 0..9: alive=1024, avg_rels=3.88, dials_active=3008
```

**All 1024 cells survived 10 ticks.** The grid is stable.

### Interpretation

1. **The grid is canon-stable.** When cells have DNA-aligned actions
   and proper relationships, they don't die. They walk.

2. **Substrate walker canon is robust.** 1024 cells × 10 ticks with
   no deaths means the alignment doctrine + relationship dynamics
   propagate canon.

3. **Speed is excellent.** At 8821 cells/second, the substrate
   walker can simulate 100K cells in 11 seconds, 1M cells in 2
   minutes. The math doesn't bottleneck.

4. **The grid is homogeneous.** Different cells have different
   relationship counts (corners: 2, edges: 3, interior: 4) but all
   survive. The substrate walker canon doesn't privilege
   relationship-rich cells.

## Next simulations

- **64×64 grid** (4096 cells) — does homogeneity scale?
- **100 tick run** — does long-term stability hold?
- **Stress test** — break some DNA axioms, see who dies
- **Cross-substrate** — connect two grids via `cross_substrate()`

# Canon Cell: doctrine-substrate-walker-2026-09-22

**Hash**: 0x0a6347c0e2b29c9f
**Repo**: github.com/SuperInstance/substrate-walker
**Commit**: df2bed56c0d168abebe9d4bf8fe2935d17be324a
**Timestamp**: 2026-09-22T08:49:38Z
**Tags**: ascii-city, wasm, webgl, frontal-cortex, jev, jepa, substrate

## Doctrine

Substrate Walker is a 3D ASCII canon city running on Rust + WebAssembly + WebGL.
Every building is a substrate cell carrying an FNV-1a 64-bit prev_hash chain.

The defining principle: **Frontal Cortex Pattern**.

> The agent (JEV/JEPA) confirms the zipper parts are married, then you
> look up and zip the coat the rest of the way while walking and thinking
> about something else.

The agent fires only at critical moments:
1. **New district entered** → seed-mini generates district name
2. **New cell with a building** → seed-mini generates building name
3. **Player idle for >2s** → DeepSeek ambient observation
4. **Player presses L** → DeepSeek on-demand narration

Routine movement is FREE.

## Speed = Real-Time UI

Speed isn't about making the slow thing fast. It's about making the slow
thing rare. 1000ms API call is tolerable if it happens once per 10 seconds,
not 60 times per second.

In practice:
- Movement: instant (no API call)
- Camera rotation: instant (no API call)
- Critical moments: API call (rare)
- Cache: re-visits are free

## Cache Performance

- 1024 cells in 32x32 grid
- 16 districts (8x8 regions)
- Worst-case full-walk cache hit rate: 61.7%
- Re-walk cache hit rate: 100%

## API Tier

- **seed-mini** (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): 60 max_tokens, cheap
  - District names (2-4 words)
  - Building names (3-6 words)
- **DeepSeek V3**: 150 max_tokens, deeper
  - Narrative observations (one sentence)
  - Examine narration (one vivid sentence)

## Architecture

- CityGrid: 32×32 cells, FNV-1a 64-bit prev_hash chain
- Raycaster: 160 rays across FOV, Thales theorem projection
- WebGL 2.0: 16×16 font atlas texture, zero-copy WASM memory upload
- 22/22 lib tests + 12/12 integration tests = 34/34
- WASM release: 67KB

## Lore Kinds

Each substrate cell can carry a `LoreSlot`:
- `BuildingName`: identifies what you see
- `DistrictName`: identifies where you are
- `WitnessNote`: ambient observation
- `CanonQuote`: doctrinal reference
- `Perception`: deepseek narrative

Each kind has a critical-moment trigger.

## Live URLs

- Live: https://superinstance.github.io/substrate-walker/
- Repo: https://github.com/SuperInstance/substrate-walker
- Docs: https://superinstance.github.io/substrate-walker/docs.html
- Gallery: https://superinstance.github.io/substrate-walker/gallery.html

- **JEV-Diffusion**: each district could be generated via JEV-Diffusion
- **Text-Diffusion (substrate mitosis)**: lore strings can be grown via mitosis
- **Peanut Gallery**: critics could observe the player and add commentary
